test_cases.title: Seeded ingestion row returns a timezone-aware last_successful_run_at
test_cases.given: system_metadata holds a row with key='ingestion' and a known last_successful_run_at
test_cases.then: it returns that timestamp as a timezone-aware datetime equal to the seeded value
test_cases.objective: Verify the accessor reads the system_metadata singleton and returns last_successful_run_at as a timezone-aware datetime matching the seeded row, establishing the freshness-api contract's field and type for its five consumers.
preconditions: Test database migrated to head via `alembic upgrade head` (BED-01's 001_initial_schema creates system_metadata)
system_metadata seeded with exactly one row: key='ingestion', last_successful_run_at=2026-09-03T09:15:00+00:00
A fresh accessor instance (or cleared module cache) so the read is a cache miss, not a warm hit from a prior case
steps: Call the freshness accessor against the test database session
expected_results: The returned value is a datetime instance
Its tzinfo is not None and its UTC offset resolves to +00:00 — the DateTime(timezone=True) column round-trips aware, not naive
No warning-level log event is emitted on this path

test_cases.title: Absent ingestion row raises the verbatim never-run message and logs a warning
test_cases.given: system_metadata has no row with key='ingestion' (migrated but never ingested)
test_cases.then: it raises with the exact message 'ingestion job may not have run yet' sourced from the module constant, and emits one warning-level log event
test_cases.objective: Verify the row-absent path is a first-class, exactly-worded outcome: the raised message is byte-identical to the module constant that the log event also uses, so the string cannot drift between the two or across refactors (research risk #2 — five downstream consumers may log or match it).
preconditions: system_metadata contains no row with key='ingestion' (table empty, or seeded only with unrelated keys)
A fresh accessor instance so the absent-row state is actually queried, not masked by a cached value from another case
Log capture attached at WARNING level over the accessor module's logger
steps: Assert the precondition: a select on system_metadata where key='ingestion' returns no row
Attach a WARNING-level log capture over the accessor module's logger
Call the freshness accessor and capture the raised exception
expected_results: The call raises rather than returning None or a sentinel datetime

The raised message contains 'ingestion job may not have run yet' byte-exactly — asserted against the imported module constant, not a re-typed literal, so a change to the constant fails this case instead of silently passing
The raised error carries HTTP status 500, per BED-04-FR-1's recorded 500-over-503 choice
Exactly one WARNING-level record was emitted during the call
That record's message is the same module constant, and it carries no user identifier or request content (security NFR: no PII in logs)

test_cases.title: Warm reads stay under 10 ms p95 within the 300s TTL, then pick up the updated timestamp once it expires
test_cases.given: the accessor has been called once and the underlying row is then updated out-of-band
test_cases.when: it is called repeatedly inside the 300-second TTL and again after the TTL has elapsed
test_cases.then: the in-TTL calls serve the original value from cache at p95 < 10 ms with no further database read, and the post-TTL call returns the updated timestamp
test_cases.objective: Verify both legs of the TTL contract in one boundary case — that a warm hit does no I/O and meets the < 10 ms p95 budget (AC-3), and that apparent staleness is bounded at exactly the documented 300s rather than being indefinite (AC-4). TTL expiry is the only invalidating event, because the ingestion writer runs out-of-process and cannot invalidate an in-process cache.
preconditions: A fresh accessor instance with an empty cache
The monotonic clock the accessor reads is controllable by the test (fake/patched), so the 300s boundary is crossed without a real 5-minute wait
Database reads are countable for the duration of the case (query counter or session-level spy)
steps: Call the accessor once to populate the cache; record the database read count after this call
Update system_metadata.last_successful_run_at to 2026-09-03T09:47:00+00:00 out-of-band, simulating an out-of-process ingest write
Advance the accessor's monotonic clock by 299 seconds — inside the TTL
Call the accessor 200 times, timing each call
Advance the accessor's monotonic clock past the boundary, to 301 seconds since the populating call
expected_results: Every in-TTL call returns 2026-09-03T09:15:00+00:00 — the cached value, not the row's new value
The database read count is unchanged across all 200 in-TTL calls: the warm path performs no query
p95 of the 200 warm-read durations is < 10 ms
The post-TTL call returns 2026-09-03T09:47:00+00:00, still timezone-aware
The database read count increased by exactly 1 across the post-TTL call — one primary-key read per TTL window, not one per call
Worst-case observed staleness never exceeds the 300s TTL

budget.measured: p95 = 0.000292 ms (292 ns) over 200 warm reads; 0 SELECTs in-TTL, exactly 1 SELECT post-TTL

audit_notes: BED-04-AC-2 is covered by TC-02, whose requirement_id is the delta FR that extends it (BED-04-FR-1) rather than the AC id — FR-1 adds the module-constant, warning-log and status constraints on top of AC-2's assertion, so one case satisfies both obligations under the 3-case cap.

BED-04-AC-3 and BED-04-AC-4 are both covered by TC-03: they are the two legs of a single TTL boundary (serve-from-cache before 300s, re-read after), and testing them as one case is what makes the boundary itself — not just each side of it — the thing under test.

BED-04-NFR-security carries no numeric budget and asserts an absence (no RBAC gating on a read-only accessor), so the coverage minimum requires no typed case for it. TC-02 partially covers its no-PII-in-logs clause. A dedicated type:security case was omitted under the user-directed cap.
BED-04-NFR-accessibility is N/A — backend accessor, no UI surface in this story.

No unit-shaped cases appear here by design (test-case-generation § Scope): the accessor's internal cache mechanics belong in docs/features/BED-04/tasks.json as a pytest task, authored at /arh-plan-implementation.
